 Myron Gardner produced 14 points (5-of-7 FGs), two rebounds, three assists and four three-pointers in Monday’s win over the Rockets. 
 With Pelle Larsson (illness) out, Gardner has started Miami’s last three games. After shooting 1-of-8 from three and scoring five points in the first two games, the undrafted wing matched his career high with 14 points, shooting 4-of-5 from beyond the arc. This was a good night for Gardner, but it shouldn’t sway the opinion of fantasy managers. Larsson said before Monday’s game that he expects to play Wednesday against the Bucks, so there’s little reason to add Gardner.

 Pelle Larsson (illness) said Monday that he expects to be healthy enough to play on Wednesday against the Bucks. 
 Larsson, who’s recovering from a cold, has missed Miami’s last three games. Myron Gardner has filled the void in the starting lineup as head coach Erik Spoelstra continues to bring the struggling Andrew Wiggins off the bench. Larsson should be in the starting lineup on Wednesday if he’s available.

 Thomas Sorber (knee) underwent a procedure on his right knee on Tuesday and will be re-evaluated in 6-8 weeks. 
 Sorber, who suffered a torn ACL during his lone season at Georgetown, missed the entire 2025-26 season and has yet to make his NBA debut. Late in his return-to-play process, the Thunder center developed inflammation in the patellofemoral joint of his right knee, necessitating Tuesday’s procedure. Sorber is expected to resume on-court activities in 6-8 weeks, but this does not affect fantasy basketball.

 The Grizzlies announced on Tuesday that GG Jackson (foot) will be re-evaluated in three months. 
 Jackson suffered a broken fifth metatarsal in his right foot during Saturday’s win over the Nets. Tuesday’s surgical procedure was successful, and he’ll be re-evaluated in three months.
